The saying you never get a second chance to make a first impression couldn’t be more true during the interview process. First impressions of a company or hiring team are impactful because they shape the candidate’s initial perception about an organization. These impressions can have a lasting effect and can be difficult to shake.


First impressions and providing a positive candidate experience go hand in hand. Positive interactions between candidates and hiring teams are crucial for several reasons. Most importantly, it reflects the employer’s brand and reputation. A positive experience can enhance the organization’s image, making it more attractive to potential job seekers. It encourages candidates to speak positively about their experience, leading to referrals and a more robust and extensive talent pipeline. Candidates with great experience are more likely to accept job offers and become engaged team members, impacting the company’s overall success. Like a bad first impression, a negative interview experience can hurt the employer’s reputation and discourage talented individuals from applying or engaging with the company.


A candidate’s journey should provide insights into the company’s culture, values, and how it treats its team members. When building out MNTN’s hiring process, we kept the candidates’ experience top of mind at each step. Our goal is to excite, inform, and prepare candidates to win the interview. We do this by engaging in thoughtful conversations, providing seamless scheduling, sending interview prep to candidates, and providing timely follow-up and feedback.


One of the most impactful resources we send to our candidates to help them feel prepared is MNTN’s Base Camp. This comprehensive guide was built by the MNTN TA team to educate candidates on our story, interview process, community, benefits/perks, and frequently asked questions.


Another highlight of the MNTN candidate experience is our committed team members and communication tools that allow us to schedule interviews efficiently and effectively and send text reminders to our candidates.


We want to ensure that even if a candidate is not selected for the role, we leave a lasting impression and encourage them to consider future opportunities with MNTN. Even if you don’t end up as a MNTN team member, we still want you to feel like one with each interaction.


*Final Thoughts:*
Amy Cuddy of Harvard Business School studies the science of meeting people. She presented at PopTech about how we form first impressions. She found that when we meet individuals for the first time, we assess two things: trustworthiness and competence. She explains that you can learn to make a better first impression once you understand this. You can initiate trust by gathering information about a person’s interests—allowing them to share things about themselves. She suggests replacing your power pose with small talk the next time you prepare for an interview.


Overall, a candidate’s experience should be fun, informative, supportive, and mutually beneficial for the organization and its potential team members.
